transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Markus Li (SiriusCare Head of ML), Aisha Khan (Platform Eng), Tom Reyes (CTO)

Summary (auto): review of bench numbers vs current vendor; triage p99 tail lat and KV-cache behavior; agree on next tests and artifacts to share.

Topics: latency numbers, throughput scaling, caching, quantization, routing, security docs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: alright everybody, thanks for joining, um, we'll kick this off. quick agenda — go through the bench numbers from last week, triage the p99 spikes, decide next tests, and handoff any config for dedicated slots.
[00:18] Markus: sounds good. we had a couple of engineers pulled into other things so short notice for us but we got the dashboard pulled up.
[00:25] Priya: cool, i'm going to share the test matrix again — run A is 256 tokens, run B 512 tokens, warm vs cold cache, and then routing 100% redwood vs 75/25 split.
[00:40] Aisha: just to confirm, the incumbent baseline numbers we sent earlier — are those the latest?
[00:45] Jordan: yes those are the June baseline from CloudInfer — sorry, from the incumbent — p50 38ms, p95 180, p99 420 for 512 tokens on their managed endpoint in our lab env.
[01:02] Speaker 1 (Tom?): okay.
[01:06] Priya: Redwood's head-to-head showed p50 around 32ms, p95 ~160ms, but we saw p99 around 560ms on cold KV paths, which is higher than the incumbent in a couple of runs. so median is better, tail worse in those scenarios.
[01:25] Markus: that's exactly what we saw in prod too — most queries are fine but a small fraction hit a big delay and that breaks our real-time routing SLA.
[01:33] Priya: right. digging into it, two main suspects: first, KV cache cold misses cause a fetch and the runtime had a fallback path that adds ~200ms occasionally; second, at high conc the decoding loop sometimes stalls with quantized kernels on certain GPU kernels we selected — especially when batch sizes change erratically.
[01:56] Aisha: when you say KV cache cold, is that prefix caching or full KV? we saw large variance for short prompts.
[02:03] Priya: it's prefix + KV cell. for these tests prefix caching only warms after a couple of requests per key. in our 75/25 routing the cold share is still nontrivial.
[02:12] Jordan: quick interrup — we also noticed that the incumbent had a different batching strategy that forces fixed decode batches which reduces jitter, but increases median slightly. so it's a tradeoff.
[02:28] Tom: makes sense. any quick wins we can try this sprint?
[02:32] Priya: yes — a couple: enable aggressive prefix caching TTL for the sample keys, stabilize decoding batch sizes with a small padding window, and tweak quant profile to prefer per-layer FP16 for the attention kernels where quant caused stalls. those are config changes we can push in lab.
[02:52] Markus: will that change unit cost? we have a budget constraint.
[02:56] Jordan: good Q — Priya, you mentioned expected unit-cost delta in your note?
[02:59] Priya: preliminary, uh, enabling aggressive caching reduces token emissions on repeated prefixes which lowers cost; stabilizing batch sizes slightly ups median compute utilization but drops tail, net effect likely small (<5%) on unit cost for most workloads. quant changes could reduce compute by 10-20% but might cause occasional decoding stalls which is what we saw. We'll quantify in the expanded runs.
[03:24] Aisha: we also need to validate within our VPC model — the private deployment has different network egress which could affect p99.
[03:32] Lena: i've got the private deployment checklist and soc2 docs, i'll share after the call.
[03:36] Jordan: perfect.
[03:40] [05:00] Priya: moving into the numbers sheet — run B 512 token warm path: throughput peaked at 880 rps per 8xA10 cluster in our lab, CPU and GPU looked ~72% util, latencies p95 ~150ms. that was good.
[05:20] Markus: that's promising, our production target is sustained 700 rps with p95 under 200ms.
[05:27] Priya: right — but when we flip to the cold KV mix (about 20% cold) p99 jumps to 500-600ms which triggers your SLA violation per your notes.
[05:40] Tom: do we have traces? is it network egress or model decode?
[05:45] Priya: traced it both — for 60% of p99 cases it's a KV fetch hop, measured as an extra 180-230ms; remaining 40% are decoder stalls correlated with mixed batch sizes when a quant kernel is chosen by the runtime scheduler.
[06:05] Markus: so two levers — caching behavior and scheduling of kernels. can the runtime prefer non-quant kernels during peak to avoid stalls?
[06:12] Priya: yes, we can pin an execution profile that uses FP16 kernels for decode and fall back to quant when underutilized, it's a per-model config. that will reduce the risk of stalls but increase cost a bit.
[06:25] Jordan: and we should also test routing fallback: if a request hits a cold KV event, maybe send to incumbent fallback or to a warm pool. we demoed a 75/25 split earlier — that mitigates end-user impact.
[06:38] Aisha: is that automatic or manual? how do you decide routing?
[06:42] Priya: routing policy can be latency-first or cost-first; we can set heuristics — e.g., detect cold-key and route to warm pool/backup endpoint. there's also an automatic fallback if latency SLO is breached.
[06:55] Markus: we'd prefer automatic fallback with observability hooks to avoid manual ops.
[06:59] Jordan: makes sense. Lena, do you have notes on audit logs we promised?
[07:03] Lena: yes, i'll attach a link to the SOC2 report, plus a network architecture PDF and KMS integration guide.
[07:12] Tom: ok great.
[07:15] [09:00] Priya: next, throughput headroom — at 1k rps sustained we saw GPU queueing start to climb and tail latency moves up. but importantly, when we locked batch sizes (padding to 8) the tail stabilized even under higher concurrency.
[09:22] Markus: are there memory pressure effects with that padding?
[09:25] Priya: slight bump in GPU memory, but still well within the 48GB footprint for our model; quantized profile had less memory but more kernel jitter.
[09:36] Aisha: please quantify memory delta in the next run.
[09:38] Priya: will do.
[09:40] Jordan: We'd also like to understand cost per 1M tokens in each profile — hosted vs dedicated pricing changes.
[09:49] Jordan: quick note, pricing slide is a draft we can send, it shows dedicated slots at a discount once you commit to X hours per month.
[09:58] Markus: that is relevant — if we can guarantee load we may prefer dedicated. but we need to be sure tail is solved first.
[10:06] [12:00] Priya: on the expanded test plan: we'll run a 1k concurrent-request sweep for both 256 and 512 tokens, measure p50/p95/p99, include a synthetic cold-KV injection at 20% of requests, and compare two model profiles: FP16-stable vs quant-fast. we'll push logs and traces into the shared S3.
[12:22] Markus: how long will that run take in lab?
[12:25] Priya: roughly 6 hours of wall time for a full sweep, but each individual stage returns data in ~20–30 minutes, we'll run overnight and share artifacts.
[12:36] Tom: will that reflect our prod networking? remember our prod VPC to cloud egress adds ~20–30ms.
[12:43] Priya: good call — we can add an egress latency simulation to the test harness to approximate your VPC delta. please send the values.
[12:51] Jordan: Markus, can you share typical egress lat numbers?
[12:55] Markus: sure, 28ms on average, peaking 45ms. we'll add that in the ticket.
[13:02] [15:00] Aisha: another question — what about model version pinning? we need deterministic behavior for canary rollouts.
[15:07] Priya: Redwood supports pinning by model-version and we can orchestrate canary traffic split, plus automatic rollback if regressions are detected. we'll include the rollout playbook as part of the handoff.
[15:20] Jordan: also to note: we saw one anomalous p99 where the runtime did a fallback to a CPU path because the GPU kernel crashed on that instance; SE will look at health checks to prevent that.
[15:34] Priya: yes that's on my list. config change will disable auto-fallback to CPU for that kernel family until we have a stable quant patch.
[15:43] Markus: ok.
[15:45] [20:00] Tom: any regulatory concerns? data residency?
[20:04] Lena: SiriusCare requested EU data residency for some patients; Redwood's private deployment supports that, and we have KMS integration and audit logs. i'll send the compliance pack.
[20:17] Markus: can we get retention controls for logs?
[20:20] Lena: yes, retention and redaction settings are configurable.
[20:24] Priya: back to bench — i'll also run a test where we artificially inflate cold-key frequency to 40% to see worst-case tail.
[20:32] Jordan: good. that will help size warm pool and decide if fallback routing is needed.
[20:40] [35:00] Priya: quick note on benchmarking methodology — we will attach raw traces, a sanitized flamegraph of GPU kernels, and a spreadsheet with per-run metadata. be aware transcription of hostnames in traces may be anonymized.
[35:18] Aisha: ok.
[35:20] Markus: what about the competitor comparison — did you run Megapipe?
[35:24] Priya: we ran a small head-to-head against Megapipe's managed offering earlier — medians similar, and their p99 for our workload was ~480ms — Redwood is close in median but we still need to close tail.
[35:37] Jordan: worth noting Megapipe uses fixed decode batches which hides jitter but increases median.
[35:44] Tom: anything else?
[35:48] Priya: i'll enumerate the config diffs after the meeting. main actions: extended load test, add egress sim, quant vs FP16 sweep, warm-pool sizing, and routing/fallback playbook.
[36:02] Jordan: great. let's run through explicit next steps.
[36:06] [45:00] Action recap (verbal):
- Priya to run expanded 1k sweep (512/256 tokens, KV cold 20% and 40%) and produce p50/p95/p99 + traces by 2026-07-28.
- Markus to share prompt set & token distribution by 2026-07-23.
- Jordan to send draft pricing and dedicated slot request by 2026-07-24.
- Lena to share SOC2 + network architecture + KMS guide by 2026-07-25.

[46:30] Tom: let's tentatively schedule a deep dive once we have the expanded artifacts, maybe 7/29?
[46:38] Jordan: 7/29 works for us. we'll lock time after artifacts land.
[46:42] Markus: thanks all.
[46:45] Aisha: thanks.
[46:47] Lena: thanks, i'll post the links.
[46:50] Priya: thanks everyone, we'll get started on the runs and share results.
[46:55] Jordan: meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
